Consequently, the product will most likely be classified as Class IIa in both jurisdictions unless its intended use or risk profile warrants a higher class.

For a Class IIa SaMD, conformity assessment requires a notified body to review the technical documentation, quality management system (QMS), and clinical evaluation. The manufacturer must compile a Declaration of Conformity and affix the CE mark before placing the product on the EU market. Post‑Brexit, the UK has introduced the UKCA marking under the UK MDR 2021; however, transitional arrangements allow CE‑marked devices to continue being sold in Great Britain until 30 June 2025 (subject to a “dual‑marking” requirement for certain high‑risk categories).
